# package fxstore

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/uafx/fxstore"
```

Package fxstore is the durable storage of the UAFX persistent connections: the ConnectionEndpoints an AutomationComponent restores after a restart (OPC 10000-81 §5.5.5, §6.6.2) and, later, the state of a ConnectionManager. The application supplies the backend, a [Store](#type-store); the library owns what it writes there, its format and its migration. The package has no dependency outside the standard library and go-opcua.

A Store is a byte key-value map with an atomic [Store.Apply](#func-store-apply). Its contract separates three outcomes of a write: committed (nil), definitely not committed (an error that wraps ErrNotCommitted) and unknown (any other error). A [Domain](#type-domain) is what the library writes through: one namespace of keys with a meta key that carries a revision and a batch identity, so that an unknown outcome can be settled later by a confirming write, and a fence that refuses new writes until it is.

[MemoryStore](#type-memorystore) implements the contract in memory for tests and for applications that want its protocols without persistence: it survives no restart. [FileStore](#type-filestore) is a reference backend on a local directory. The contract tests of package storetest check any backend.

The design is docs/design/uafx-persistent-connections.md §3.

### type Domain

```go
type Domain struct {

	// committed state, full keys, meta included

	// relative keys

}
```

Domain is one namespace of a Store as the library writes it: every Apply also writes the meta key of the namespace with the next revision and a random batch identity, so that Load tells which batch the visible state ends with.

An Apply with an unknown outcome fences the domain: later Applies fail with ErrFenced, without writing, until Settle establishes the outcome (design §3.3, §3.5). Settle loads the state, finds the revision it ends with, and confirms it with an Apply that writes only the meta key on top of it: when that commits, the loaded state is durable (prefix durability) and the unknown batch's outcome is known. A confirming Apply that is unknown itself is remembered with what its base contained, so repeated ambiguous confirmations never lose the identity or the evidence of the original batch.

A Domain is safe for concurrent use; its writes are serialized. It starts no goroutines: the caller runs Settle, typically with a backoff.

#### func OpenDomain

```go
func OpenDomain(ctx context.Context, s Store, o DomainOptions) (*Domain, error)
```

OpenDomain loads the namespace o.Namespace of s. It fails when the store cannot be loaded, holds keys outside the namespace, is over o.Limits, belongs to another owner (ErrForeignOwner), has a newer schema (ErrSchema) or a meta key that does not decode (ErrCorrupt).

#### func (Domain) Apply

```go
func (d *Domain) Apply(ctx context.Context, b Batch) (Outcome, error)
```

Apply writes b, its keys relative to the namespace, with the next revision. It returns the outcome and, unless committed, an error: a fenced domain is NotCommitted with ErrFenced.

#### func (Domain) Require

```go
func (d *Domain) Require(ctx context.Context, b Batch) (Outcome, error)
```

Require writes b like Apply and, unless the write commits, owes it: the domain stays fenced until Settle has written it. It is for the writes that make the store follow a change the runtime made already (a removal), which must not be lost.

#### func (Domain) Schema

```go
func (d *Domain) Schema() uint16
```

Schema returns the schema of the loaded records (0 for an empty store).

#### func (Domain) Settle

```go
func (d *Domain) Settle(ctx context.Context) (bool, error)
```

Settle establishes the outcome of an unresolved write and writes the required ones. It returns true when the domain is no longer fenced, and the error of the step that kept it fenced. It writes nothing when the domain is not fenced.

#### func (Domain) State

```go
func (d *Domain) State() map[string][]byte
```

State returns the records of the domain as the domain knows them committed, by key relative to the namespace, without the meta key. While a write is unresolved it is the state before that write.

#### func (Domain) Status

```go
func (d *Domain) Status() DomainStatus
```

Status returns the state of the domain.

### type FileStore

```go
type FileStore struct {

	// the data file as last written or read
	// state may differ from the data file

}
```

FileStore is a Store in a local directory: a lock file and one data file with the whole state. Apply writes the new state to a temporary file, fsyncs it, renames it over the data file and fsyncs the directory, so a committed Apply survives a crash of the process and, where the file system honours fsync, a power loss (prefix durability: every Apply rewrites the whole state). An error before the rename is ErrNotCommitted; an error at or after it, the directory fsync included, is an unknown outcome.

One FileStore owns its directory: Open takes an exclusive lock (flock on Unix, an exclusive open of the lock file on Windows) and holds it until Close; a second Open, in this process or another, fails with ErrLocked. It is safe for concurrent use; Applies are serialized.

Platform limits: on Windows a directory cannot be fsynced, so a renamed data file survives a crash of the process but its rename is only as durable as the file system's metadata journal makes it: Durability is DurabilityProcessCrash there, DurabilityPowerLoss elsewhere. Network file systems (NFS, SMB) and file systems that ignore fsync or advisory locks are not supported: neither the lock nor the durability holds on them. Platforms without flock (other than Unix systems with it and Windows) cannot open a FileStore.

The directory is created 0700 if missing; a directory that the group or others may write is refused, and the files are created 0600. The data is stored as written: an application that needs encryption at rest wraps the Store.

FileStore is meant for the size of a configuration (a few MiB): Apply is O(state).

#### func OpenFile

```go
func OpenFile(dir string, limits Limits) (*FileStore, error)
```

OpenFile opens the FileStore in dir, creating dir and an empty store if missing. It removes a temporary file a crash left. It fails with ErrLocked when another writer has the store, with ErrCorrupt when the data file does not decode, and with ErrLimit when it is over limits.

### type MemoryStore

```go
type MemoryStore struct {
	// Limits bound the state; the zero value is the defaults.
	Limits Limits

}
```

MemoryStore is a Store in memory: it implements the logical transactions of the contract (atomic Apply, the outcomes, Close, Limits) and nothing else. It is not durable: its state goes with the process. Use it for tests, and for the protocols of the persistent connections without persistence.

A MemoryStore is safe for concurrent use. Its zero value is ready to use with the default Limits.

#### func (MemoryStore) Apply

```go
func (m *MemoryStore) Apply(ctx context.Context, b Batch) error
```

Apply applies b atomically. It never returns an unknown outcome.

func (m *MemoryStore) Close() error

### type Store

```go
type Store interface {
	// Load returns the visible state: every key with its value. The
	// returned map and slices belong to the caller.
	Load(ctx context.Context) (map[string][]byte, error)
	// Apply makes the puts and deletes of b durable, all or none. It
	// returns nil when they are committed, an error that wraps
	// ErrNotCommitted when nothing of b was made durable, and any other
	// error when the outcome is unknown.
	//
	// A committed Apply makes durable the whole state it was applied to,
	// including every earlier batch Load could see at that moment (prefix
	// durability).
	Apply(ctx context.Context, b Batch) error
	// Close releases the store. Load and Apply after Close return
	// ErrClosed.
	Close() error
}
```

Store keeps the durable state of one AutomationComponent server or one ConnectionManager. One process owns it: the one that opened it.

The methods are safe for concurrent use; Applies are serialized.
